Text: Java uses {{c1::Type Erasure}} to maintain backwards compatibility, replacing type parameters with their bounds or {{c2::Object}} in bytecode.
Extra: This ensures that pre-generic legacy code and new generic code can run together on the same JVM.

Text: Java generics are {{c1::invariant}}, meaning `List<Integer>` is not a subtype of `List<Number>`, which prevents adding {{c2::incompatible types}} at runtime.
Extra: To restore API flexibility, wildcards like `? extends T` and `? super T` are used.

Text: The PECS mnemonic stands for {{c1::Producer Extends, Consumer Super}}, directing the use of wildcards for collection parameters.
Extra: `? extends T` is for producing/reading, `? super T` is for consuming/writing.

Text: Raw types bypass compile-time safety checks, causing the JVM to throw a {{c1::ClassCastException}} at runtime during element retrieval.
Extra: Raw types should only be used for backward compatibility with pre-Java 5 libraries.

Text: Generics do not support primitive types because primitives do not inherit from {{c1::Object}} and cannot be stored in reference slots.
Extra: The JVM designates reference slots only for object references.

Text: Generic array creation is forbidden because arrays are {{c1::reified}} at runtime, whereas generic type parameters are {{c2::erased}}.
Extra: The compiler forbids `new T[10]` to prevent bypassing array type checks.

Text: Performing `obj instanceof List<String>` is illegal; you must check using {{c1::List<?>}} or raw {{c2::List}} because generic arguments are erased.
Extra: The wildcard check is safer and cleaner than using raw types.

Text: In multiple generic bounds, the {{c1::class bound}} must be declared first, followed by {{c2::interface bounds}}: `<T extends Number & Comparable<T>>`.
Extra: Placing an interface bound before a class bound results in a compile error.

Text: You cannot overload methods that differ only in generic parameters because they erase to the {{c1::same bytecode signature}}.
Extra: For example, `void process(List<String> list)` and `void process(List<Integer> list)` both erase to `void process(List list)`.

Text: To instantiate a generic class type parameter `T`, you must pass a {{c1::Class<T>}} token and use {{c2::reflection}}.
Extra: Writing `new T()` is a compile error because `T` is erased to Object or its bounds.

Text: Adding a typed element (except `null`) to a list with an upper-bounded wildcard `List<? extends Number>` is {{c1::forbidden}} by the compiler.
Extra: Because the actual type could be `List<Double>`, adding an `Integer` would cause type unsafety.

Text: Static fields of type parameter types are forbidden because static fields are {{c1::shared across all instances}} of the class.
Extra: Class instantiations like `Box<String>` and `Box<Integer>` share the same class metadata.
